title: What Changes on the Real Robot: Delay, a Slow Actuator and Friction in the Loop, the Delay a Joint Can Stand, and Gains Chosen Against a Spread of Robots

artifact.note: the gap between a simulator and the real joint: a joint with inertia, a PD law, a torque limit and friction, with the real robot's differences added to the simulation (a delay in the command, a lag in the actuator that makes the torque follow the command with a time constant); the step response of that loop (whether it settles, its overshoot and its settling time); the largest delay it can stand with given gains (found by halving an interval); and the share of a spread of randomly drawn robots (inertia, delay and lag each over a range) for which a set of gains settles, to show that gains chosen for the nominal robot can fail on the real one, and that a gentler set has a margin
